extracted.intended_audience: USPTO-registered patent practitioners, disciplinary counsel, and law office managers
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order describing stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions in a USPTO disciplinary matter against a registered patent practitioner; documents the regulatory violations, mitigating factors, and the specific sanctions and procedural requirements applicable to the practitioner. Useful for understanding professional-responsibility standards and sanctioning practice under USPTO rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction for disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes statutory and regulatory basis for OED authority to bring and settle disciplinary proceedings against registered practitioners; referenced to justify the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.26
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent have submitted a proposed settlement agreement that meets the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.26 to resolve the pending disciplinary complaint without a hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement may resolve current and certain future disciplinary actions (here, all discipline arising from Respondent's representation of ISC-referred clients for the same or similar acts/omissions). The Final Order implements agreed stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of ISC-referred clients
rubrics_metrics.description: "ISC-referred Clients" is defined as all clients referred to Respondent by the Invention Submission Corporation ("ISC") and for whom Respondent provided legal services before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies the class of clients whose representation and the associated conduct form the basis of the complaint and scope of settlement coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c) — duty to inform clients of Office correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation by failing to inform clients of correspondence received from the Office when the correspondence (i) could have a significant effect on a matter pending before the Office, (ii) is received by the practitioner on behalf of a client or former client, and (iii) is correspondence of which a reasonable practitioner would believe under the circumstances the client or former client should be notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites the practitioner's failure to timely inform ISC-referred clients of Office actions and to explain their significance as a breach of this duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.62(a) — accepting referred clients without consent after full disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation by accepting referred clients from a referring entity without the consent of the referred client after full disclosure, including not adequately describing the escrow and payment arrangement for patent legal services performed for referred clients, where the exercise of the practitioner's independent professional judgment on behalf of the referred client will be or reasonably may be affected by the practitioner's own financial, business, property, or personal interests (e.g., Respondent's business relationship with the referring entity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires full disclosure of referral/financial arrangements and informed client consent where the practitioner's independent judgment may be affected by a business relationship with the referring entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.66(a) — duty to decline employment when conflicts impair judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation by not declining employment from a referring entity where the exercise of Respondent's independent professional judgment on behalf of a client will be or is likely to be adversely affected by the acceptance of the proffered employment or if it would be likely to involve Respondent in representing differing interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioner must decline representation if the engagement would likely impair independent judgment or create conflicting representations, absent appropriate measures such as full disclosure and consent where allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) — failing to act on legal matters entrusted to practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation by failing to act on legal matters entrusted to him, including not communicating with referred clients adequately and in a timely manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited behaviors include allowing applications to become abandoned without client consent and not providing sufficient legal advice when abandonment occurred; this duty encompasses timely communication and diligent prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required attorney-client communication and case management practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must speak directly with clients about inventions, the legal services to be rendered, patentability opinions, pre-filing discussions, timely inform clients of Office actions, explain the significance of Office actions, counsel on options for responding, advise about legal consequences (including of non-response), assist in making decisions on Office actions, and keep clients fully and timely apprised of application status directly and/or through adequate supervision of staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order details these expectations as the baseline conduct the Respondent failed to meet; deficiencies in these areas constitute professional misconduct under the cited regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervision of staff and prevention of abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must adequately supervise staff to ensure clients are kept apprised and that prosecution deadlines are met; failure to supervise that results in abandoned applications or actions taken without client knowledge violates professional obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifically notes Respondent allowed certain applications to become abandoned without clients' consent and failed to keep clients apprised through adequate supervision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors to be considered in imposing discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Mitigating considerations include no prior disciplinary history during nearly fifteen years of registration, evidence of positive changes in law office management and client communication, cooperation with OED and Office of the Solicitor, and agreement to make restitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors were considered by the OED Director in reaching the settlement and determining the nature/extent of sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension as a sanction and its duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended for a period of sixty (60) months from the practice of patent, trademark, and non-patent law before the USPTO commencing on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the principal disciplinary remedy imposed for the violations found; other conditions and possible early reinstatement rules are set out separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to practice to facilitate compliance with § 11.58(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date the Final Order is signed and expiring thirty (30) days after that date for the sole purpose of facilitating compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-term limited recognition allows the practitioner to take necessary administrative steps required by the suspension rules (e.g., notifying clients) in accordance with § 11.58(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: § 11.58 governs duties of suspended practitioners (e.g., notice to clients, return of papers, protection of client interests); compliance is a condition of suspension and of any petition for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restitution obligations and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall, within forty-five (45) days of the date the Final Order is signed, make restitution in the total amount of $8,085.00 by remitting $1,155.00 to each of the seven ISC-referred clients identified (with two named clients treated as one client for restitution purposes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent must provide an affidavit and corroborating documents (e.g., copies of checks and correspondence to clients) within sixty (60) days establishing compliance with the restitution requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from Customer Numbers 30,245 and 78,285 and the public key infrastructure ("PKI") certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent shall not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on applying for Customer Number while suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A procedural safeguard to prevent practice before the Office during suspension by re-creating electronic access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for reinstatement timing and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time after fifteen (15) months from the date the Final Order is signed, Respondent may file a petition for reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 requesting reinstatement effective prior to the expiration of the 60-month suspension; reinstatement requires proof under § 11.60(c) that (1) Respondent has the good moral character and reputation, competency, and learning in law required under 37 C.F.R. § 11.7 for admission, (2) resumption of practice will not be detrimental to the administration of justice or subversive to the public interest, (3) compliance with the provisions of the Final Order for the full period of suspension, and (4) compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the earliest date to petition for early reinstatement (after 15 months) and enumerates the regulatory requirements the petitioner must meet to obtain reinstatement under USPTO rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation following reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall serve a period of probation commencing on the date the Final Order is signed and ending forty-five (45) months after the OED Director reinstates Respondent pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 ("Respondent's probationary period").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions during probation are enforceable; failure to comply may trigger Order to Show Cause procedures and additional suspension or amendment of the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause procedure for probation or noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes Respondent, during probation, failed to comply with any provision of the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to Respondent's last address of record, grant 15 days to respond, and thereafter may deliver the matter to the USPTO Director requesting amendment of the Final Order (e.g., require serving the full 60-month suspension) or immediate suspension for up to 45 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outlines the two-step enforcement and potential escalation mechanism (OED process then referral to USPTO Director) and the possible consequences for probationary violations or noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order in the OED Reading Room and publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette; pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director shall also give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where Respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandated dissemination of disciplinary information to appropriate agencies and the public; the Official Gazette notice summarizes the violations and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office's reservation of rights for further discipline and use of record
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the settlement prevents the Office from seeking discipline against Respondent under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34 through 11.57 for misconduct upon which an Order to Show Cause is issued; the Office may consider the record of this proceeding, including the Final Order, in future disciplinary proceedings as an aggravating factor or to rebut representations by or on Respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The settlement does not grant immunity from future discipline for the same or similar misconduct and permits the record to be used in later proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: No automatic stay of amended or suspension orders during review
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO Director enters an order amending the Final Order (e.g., to require serving the full sixty-month suspension) or immediately suspending Respondent for up to 45 months, and Respondent seeks review of that action, any such review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the USPTO Director's order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures that administrative review does not delay enforcement of amended discipline or immediate suspension.
